verifications.claim: As of mid-March 2026, NASA is tracking several small near-Earth asteroids.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Next Five Asteroid Approaches' lists several small asteroids (29-53 feet) approaching late March 2026; R1/R2: 'one of several close approaches cataloged by NASA each year'; R4: 'five asteroids approaching Earth today'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm NASA tracks several small NEAs around mid-March 2026 timeframe.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'An asteroid the size of a bus'

verifications.claim: Asteroid 2026 EG1 is approximately 20-40 feet in size.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'estimated to be about 40 feet wide'
verifications.reasoning: 40 feet falls within the approximate 20-40 feet range.

verifications.claim: Asteroid 2026 EG1 safely passed within 198,000 miles on March 13, 2026.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'passed about 198,000 miles from Earth'; 'poses no threat'; 'late Thursday night'
verifications.reasoning: Distance and safety directly supported; specific date March 13 not mentioned (only 'late Thursday night').

verifications.claim: Asteroid 2026 EG1 passed closer than the moon on March 13, 2026.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'passed roughly 198,000 miles from Earth — closer than the moon’s average distance of about 239,000 miles'; 'late Thursday night'
verifications.reasoning: Closer than moon directly supported; specific date March 13 omitted.

verifications.claim: Routine close approaches are closely monitored by the NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)' Asteroid Watch; R4: 'NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)'; R1/R2: 'NASA’s Center for Near-Earth Object Studies' (part of JPL)
verifications.reasoning: JPL explicitly linked to monitoring close approaches.

verifications.claim: None of the small near-Earth asteroids tracked by NASA as of mid-March 2026 pose an immediate threat.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'poses no threat'; 'the vast majority do not pose an impact risk'; R3 lists small asteroids with no threat mentioned
verifications.reasoning: General no threat for small objects and specific example supported, but not explicitly 'none... immediate threat' for all tracked in mid-March.

verifications.claim: No dangerous impacts from the small near-Earth asteroids tracked by NASA as of mid-March 2026 are predicted for the next century.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'NASA doesn't predict any dangerous asteroids in the next 100 years'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement covers no dangerous impacts next century, applicable to tracked small asteroids.
